html:
An Egyptian feminist and nationalist who founded the Egyptian Feminist Union in 1923. She is best remembered for taking off her face veil in public in Cairo that same year.

Born to a rich family in Upper Egypt, she grew up in the secluded women's quarters of a Cairo household and was married young to an older cousin. She educated herself, and in the early 1900s she began to organise lectures and charities for women.

In the 1919 revolution against British rule she helped lead women's street protests and the women's wing of the Wafd, the nationalist party of Saad Zaghlul. When she returned from an international women's congress in Rome in 1923, she lifted her veil as she stepped off the train in Cairo. Many women followed her lead in the years after.

Her union pressed for votes for women, schooling for girls, a higher marriage age and limits on polygamy. In 1945 she helped found the Arab Feminist Union. Egyptian women won the vote in 1956, after her death.
sum: An Egyptian feminist and nationalist who founded the Egyptian Feminist Union in 1923. She is best remembered for taking off her face veil in public in Cairo that same year.
